correctness.rationale: For the fixed two-bin code, write D=diag(α_i) and b=(I−D)Ws/2. The two prescribed affine transitions imply (I−D²)x⁺=(D−I)b and hence uniquely x⁺=−(I+D)⁻¹b and x⁻=−x⁺. Since (Ws)_i=s_i(1−2c_i), each nonzero coordinate has its required sign exactly when the total opposite-camp row weight c_i exceeds 1/2. Equality forces a zero coordinate and fails strictness; a lower value gives the wrong sign. The successful branch is strictly inside the cube, with |x_i⁺|<1/2; any sup-norm ball of radius below the minimum sign margin maps into its partner ball and distances contract at rate max α_i. The witness has c_i=3/4 for all four rows and W² entrywise positive, giving nonzero ±(1−α)s/[4(1+α)] for each 0<α<1. In the source, every positive effective audience weight is below one, so the leverage ratio exceeds one and Theorem 4 with two bins gives the fixed thresholds (−1,0,1) and means ±1/2 for every inertia. No tie rule is used. The claim about shrinking neighborhoods is about the exhibited local balls, not the entire basin. The supplied finite rational tests were inspected, not executed; the branch proof establishes the quantified statement.

originality.rationale: The significant overlap is persistent switching in the exact lead model and attracting two-camp cycles in related models. The lead paper leaves the fixed-topology/fixed-quantizer high-inertia claim as a conjecture after a low-inertia numerical example. They do not give the strictly sign-consistent two-branch criterion in this equilibrium model or contradict that conjecture by the same mechanism. This is a best-of-knowledge finding, not a novelty claim about oscillations generally.

value.rationale: The exact cut condition is a reusable diagnostic for this fixed communication protocol, but the strongest scientific value is the fixed primitive-network counterexample to a specific open convergence prediction. It shows that persistence is not an artifact of bipartiteness, low inertia or threshold initial states: the public orbit persists for arbitrarily high inertia with an open set of starting states even though the private oscillation amplitude goes to zero. No claim is made about all recurrence, heterogeneous high-inertia convergence under added assumptions, or empirical networks.
